title.narrative: Responding to urgent needs of migrants, displaced persons and refugees in Central America 2026

description.narrative:
A comprehensive humanitarian response that combines direct assistance, psychosocial care and legal support, promoting regional coordination and the exchange of good practices to advance towards lasting solutions.
The Jesuit Network with Migrants in Central America (RJM-CA) is an interprovincial and intersectoral effort whose work focuses on migration, forced displacement and refuge. It is made up of national offices of the Jesuit Migrant Service (SJM), university programmes, parishes, Fe y Alegría and social works of the Central American Province of the Society of Jesus (PROCAM), together with other allied bodies.
The work of the RJM C.A. has continued its intervention through comprehensive and regional accompaniment, offering protection to those who leave or transit to the north of the region or remain in C.A. countries, forced to leave their homes due to political persecution, widespread violence, structural poverty and the effects of climate change. But also, in favour of the growing number of people expelled from the United States, forcibly returned to their country of origin, uprooted, without a social network, revictimised and unprotected, facing double vulnerability, being "foreigners in their own land" and in favour of those who were transferred to third countries, adding to the populations stranded in transit countries, unable to continue or return, in a situation of helplessness and insecurity in their countries of origin, finding themselves in legal and social limbo
